# One image, two placements (offline) - generated by build_tapes.py from clips.py; do not edit by hand
# SA lines only: render with digital-demand-factory/screen-demos/generate_two_voice.py

[intro]
SA: "This clip proves one claim. The application core and the container image are the same on two Kubernetes clusters: Amazon EKS Auto Mode in a Region, and kind running on this laptop as an on-premises stand-in. What differs is deployment configuration, identity, and the database each cluster uses."

[screen_01]
SA: "Both clusters apply the same Kustomize base. Each overlay adds what belongs to its placement. The Region overlay adds an arm64 node pool, and a Network Load Balancer that only accepts allowed source addresses. The on-premises overlay adds a NodePort service, a network policy, and a CloudNativePG PostgreSQL cluster."
SA: "The runtime file only sets a label. APP_RUNTIME tells the health endpoint which placement answered. Nothing in the application branches on it."

[screen_02]
SA: "This is the capture from the twenty-eighth of September rebuild, not a live call. Both targets report the same core fingerprint as this checkout, and both pods run the same image digest as the rebuilt image."
SA: "The core fingerprint compares business files. The pod image digest compares built images. Neither result means that these two placements share data or can fail over automatically."

[screen_03]
SA: "The same image does not mean the same deployment. The Region selects DynamoDB. kind selects PostgreSQL. Each cluster has its own data, its own identity, and its own network path. The composition root reads this file once at startup and wires the matching adapter. The domain and use cases never learn which one they got."

[outro]
SA: "Here is what this does not prove. It is not failover, because the two clusters do not share data and nothing switches traffic between them. It is not data residency, which needs a policy for stored data, backups, logs, access and transfers, plus evidence that they stay inside it. And kind on one laptop node is not a production on-premises cluster."
SA: "What it does prove is narrower and useful: you can place the same image in either location without touching the business code. One core, one image, deliberate placements."
